question: Remove the actual B-to-C memory callbacks without retaining a second access path or changing existing lease failure semantics.
procedure: Read complete B lease, access and location implementations; inspect provider installer, session admission wrappers and DOSWOW directory copy; search src consumers separately from tests. No product edits.
current_chain: C/F caller -> B guest_memory_access or guest_location
B lease acquire hydrates via installed C read callback, including WRITE-only leases
B lease release validates slot/epoch, optionally invokes C write, then always frees consumed valid lease
F mvdm_softpc_guest_memory_begin installs C SAS callbacks; F session gates ACTIVE admission
B copied access holds shared copy_lock while invoking C; end holds exclusive lock before freeing slots

findings.evidence: guest_location.c has ten public operations: from_far_value and set_real_mode are scalar; read_far, acquire_far, read_u16, copy_c_string, copy_to_guest, acquire, acquire_vm and release reach lease/SAS.
findings.conclusion: P19 actual implementation relocation removed F providers, but those eight functions still indirectly depend on C. Do not treat B placement as architectural closure.

findings.evidence: guest_memory_lease_acquire invokes context->read for every nonempty lease regardless of access.
findings.conclusion: A split must still hydrate write-only leases before publication. Do not optimize away that read or change failure conditions as part of ownership migration.

findings.evidence: A valid release frees and zeroes the slot even if provider write fails; foreign/stale slots return without dereference or consumption.
findings.conclusion: C must validate through B before touching lease fields, perform write when required, then unconditionally consume that validated lease. Preserve result and no-retry ownership.

findings.evidence: Shared copy_lock spans provider call; provider end takes exclusive lock. Copy-only clients do not consume the eight borrowed slots.
findings.conclusion: Split lock/epoch scope from machine access, holding the existing lock across C operation. Do not add a parallel lifetime registry or move the call outside the protection.

findings.evidence: guest_memory_access uses 4096-byte chunks and overlap-directed move; location strings stop at NUL or 16-bit offset exhaustion; acquire_vm adds explicit linear base with overflow check.
findings.conclusion: Keep these observable contracts and prior committed chunks on later failure. Do not reinterpret VM base as a host pointer or assume a particular guest OS.

B: Keep the existing eight-slot resource owner, epoch and copy/retirement lock; remove read/write/context provider fields.
Offer explicit reserve/validate/consume and begin/end copy-scope mechanics, with no callback execution. Names/signatures are a design proposal, not a new committed ABI.
Retain scalar location value construction and independent memory types. Reuse the existing host_context association; no second session/TLS.
C: Own checked SAS acquire/hydration/commit and copy operations at the existing SAS provider boundary. Candidate carrier is selected ccpusas4.c; exact insertion and mirror cost must be measured before approval.
Own location operations that perform guest access, or replace them at actual callers with the same C access path and B scalar values. Do not leave an identically complex shim in F/B.
Maintain current access symbol names/ABI where feasible; declarations consumed by C must cease importing outer private headers.
F: Keep ACTIVE admission, owner selection and shutdown timing. Call inward C access directly when a product needs guest bytes.
Remove provider installer/table when no production consumer uses it. Session wrappers may enforce product admission, but C must not call those wrappers.
Preserve DOSWOW registration epochs and original DOSWOWDATA/CDS decoding with C ownership; do not move private DOS structures into B.

consumer_cohorts: Original EMS copy/move and XMS descriptor reads
Redirector guest copy and worker copy
DOSWOW directory registration/copy and session shutdown
required_validation: Write-only read failure before lease publication
Foreign-owner/epoch-invalid release has no access or free
Failed commit still consumes valid lease exactly once
Eight-slot exhaustion and copy-only path independence
Retirement waits for active copy; no wait on unrelated guest/hardware work
Cross-page preflight, permissions and no unintended guest exception reentry
Chunk partial progress and overlapping moves
VM linear-base addition, far indirection, string terminator and offset boundary
Cross-image WOW/redirector imports resolve the same owner/context
Real EMS/XMS/DOS/WOW targeted regressions and coherent release
status: Complete-chain design refinement; exact API and measured mirror patch remain pending. No dependency IDs eliminated, no code/build/runtime changes.
